SubTopics: Interpret maps to determine that the location of mountain ranges, deep ocean trenches, volcanoes, and earthquakes occur in patterns.
Content: The map shows the location of some volcanoes in the United States.
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/1a.jpg
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/1b.jpg
What pattern is shown by the location of these volcanoes?

M.Choice: Volcanoes are usually located far from the ocean.

P.Choice: These volcanoes are centrally located around `text(one)` city.

R.Choice: The source of these volcanoes is along the West Coast.

S.Choice: Volcanoes become inactive if they are under ocean water.

SubTopics: Create an argument, using evidence from research, that human activity (farming, mining, building) can affect the land and ocean in positive and/or negative ways.
Content: Farmers often use fertilizer on their farms. Fertilizer is also used in gardens. Some people argue that fertilizer is bad for the environment.
Which effect of using fertilizer `ultext(best)` supports the argument that fertilizer is bad for the environment?

M.Choice: Fertilizer stops soil erosion in fields.

P.Choice: Fertilizer puts nutrients back into the soil.

R.Choice: Fertilizer makes plants grow bigger and faster.

S.Choice: Fertilizer disrupts the healthy balance of the soil.

SubTopics: Support an argument with evidence that plants get the materials they need for growth and reproduction chiefly through a process in which they use carbon dioxide from the air, water, and energy from the sun to produce sugars, plant materials, and waste (oxygen); and that this process is called photosynthesis.
Content: The diagram shows a food chain.

:ibox:`ultext(Food Chain)`

`text(sunlight)->text(small water plants)->text(small water animals)->text(fish)->text(seals)`
Which `ultext(three)` statements `ultext(best)` describe how energy moves through this food chain?

R.Choice: Fish get energy from small water animals.

S.Choice: Small water plants get energy from sunlight.

T.Choice: Small water plants get energy from small water animals.

SubTopics: Support an argument with evidence that plants get the materials they need for growth and reproduction chiefly through a process in which they use carbon dioxide from the air, water, and energy from the sun to produce sugars, plant materials, and waste (oxygen); and that this process is called photosynthesis.
Content: A forest food chain is shown.
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/4a.jpg
Which `ultext(two)` statements `ultext(best)` describe the movement of energy in this forest food chain?

A.Choice: The decomposer provides energy to the producer.

B.Choice: The carnivore provides energy to the producer.

C.Choice: The carnivore provides energy to the herbivore.

D.Choice: The herbivore provides energy to the carnivore.

E.Choice: The producer provides energy to the herbivore.

SubTopics: Develop models of terrestrial and aquatic food chains to describe the movement of energy among producers, herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, and decomposers.
Content: A simple marine food web is shown.
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/5a.jpg
The small fish are important in this ecosystem because they

M.Choice: give energy directly to plankton and benthic organisms.

P.Choice: get energy from predator fish and benthic organisms.

R.Choice: give energy to zooplankton and get energy from predator fish.

S.Choice: get energy from both types of plankton and give energy to predator fish.

SubTopics: Use a model to explain how the orbit of the Earth and sun cause observable patterns: a. day and night; b. changes in length and direction of shadows over a day.
Content: Organism `text(T)` became extinct about `text(250 million years)` ago. The rock strata show fossil records for Organism `text(T)` and some other organisms.
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/6a.jpg
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/6b.jpg
Because Organism `text(T)` was found in rock layers `4` and `5`, what conclusion can be made?

M.Choice: Layer `1` is the oldest of the rock strata in the diagram.

P.Choice: Layer `3` was formed less than `text(250 million years)` ago.

R.Choice: The formation of layer `5` occurred less than `text(250 million years)` ago.

S.Choice: Organism `text(T)` existed on `text(Earth)` for only a few `text(years)`.

SubTopics: Using information about the roles of organisms (producers, consumers, decomposers), evaluate how those roles in food chains are interconnected in a food web, and communicate how the organisms are continuously able to meet their needs in a stable food web.
Content: The diagram shows a food web. A food web shows feeding relationships among different organisms that live in the same habitat.
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/7a.jpg
Suddenly, there were fewer grasshoppers. Based on this food web, which population of organisms will also decrease because of this change?

SubTopics: Using information about the roles of organisms (producers, consumers, decomposers), evaluate how those roles in food chains are interconnected in a food web, and communicate how the organisms are continuously able to meet their needs in a stable food web.
Content: European starling birds are a species that was brought to the United States in the `text(1800s)`. They were used to help control insect populations. The starlings eat berries and insects such as caterpillars. A food web is shown.
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/8a.jpg
Based on the food web, which `ultext(three)` ways would the introduction of the starling `ultext(most likely)` affect this food web?

SubTopics: Use a model of a simple wave to explain regular patterns of amplitude, wavelength, and direction.
Content: Students compared `text(three)` models of waves. The models are shown.
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/9a.jpg
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/9b.jpg
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/9c.jpg
Which statement correctly compares `text(two)` of the models?

M.Choice: Wave `1` has a smaller amplitude than Wave `2`.

P.Choice: Wave `2` has a bigger amplitude than Wave `3`.

R.Choice: Wave `2` has a longer wavelength than Wave `1`.

S.Choice: Wave `3` has a shorter wavelength than Wave `2`.

SubTopics: Describe how the colors of available light sources and the bending of light waves determine what we see.
Content: A student looks at a spoon in a glass of water. The student observes that the spoon appears to be broken.
problems/TN25G4Sa/media/10a.jpg
Why does the spoon look like it is broken?

A.Choice: Light waves are bent by the water.

B.Choice: Light waves are enlarged by the water.

C.Choice: Light waves are absorbed by the water.

D.Choice: Light waves are reflected by the water.
